releaseNotes: One failure-card taxonomy, not two. emotional-design-system.md defined an emotional-card-* set describing the same violations as the experience-card-* set that EMOTIONAL_AUDIT.md actually consumes, so an agent's emitted ID depended on which file it had loaded. Founder call: converge on the consumed set. Four IDs were true duplicates and are renamed across all three files that carried them — one of them, motion-no-fallback, was literally the same name under a different prefix.

Two IDs were deliberately NOT merged, because they are distinct violations rather than duplicates. experience-card-event-missing (medium) is a spec gap — the card is implemented but ANALYTICS.md names no event. experience-card-measurement-missing (high) is a runtime gap — the card is live and the event is absent from PostHog activity. Different evidence, different severity, caught at different times. Only the namespace was wrong, so only the prefix changed. Merging them on name similarity would have deleted the runtime check.

Two more divergences surfaced only because the convergence forced a full namespace audit. emotional-card-measurement-missing was a sixth ID in the wrong namespace that the original survey missed entirely. And emotional-curve-peaks-after-paywall (definition table) versus emotional-curve-peak-after-paywall (the spelling EMOTIONAL_AUDIT.md consumes) were the same card under a singular/plural typo — resolved the same way as the taxonomy itself, by letting the consumed spelling win.

The domain now carries exactly eight failure-card IDs across three coherent namespaces: experience-card-* for card violations, emotional-curve-* for curve violations, emotional-audit-* for the audit-process one. The design-system routing table now says in a comment that the canonical YAML definitions live in emotional-experience-design.md and that its IDs must match, so the next person to add a row does not start a third set.
